clue.text: Something clutched at, with the way unprepared to take half of us

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
raw food is unprepared, not yet cooked

indicators.note: only one of the two letters of the word us is kept, here its second half

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a road for which they are not ready, taking a share of the group along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of us' keeps the S. A drowning person, the saying goes, will clutch at these.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate people proverbially clutch at straws, flimsy chances of rescue.

clue.text: Scream coming from church under landslip

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed under another is written after it

parts.note: scree is loose rock that has slipped down a slope

explanation.surface: A shriek goes up from a church buried beneath a fall of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh, high cry, a kind of scream.

clue.text: Horseman's qualification

definitions.meaning: a clause added to a document or statement that qualifies or amends it

explanation.definitionFit: A rider sits on a horse, and a rider is also a proviso tacked on to a statement.

clue.text: Resolve to have some exercise

definitions.meaning: to solve or settle a problem by thinking it through

explanation.definitionFit: To work out a problem is to resolve it; to work out is also to exercise.

clue.text: As Scott's wretch would finally be with peacekeepers dismantling guns

definitions.text: As Scott's wretch would finally be

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces come from the United Nations

indicators.note: taking the guns to pieces rearranges the letters of that word

explanation.surface: UN troops take apart weapons, leaving a villain to an unremarked end.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Scott's Lay of the Last Minstrel says the selfish wretch shall go down to the dust 'unwept, unhonour'd, and unsung'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scott's poem ends the wretch's fate with the word, meaning uncelebrated and unpraised.

clue.text: Hoon improved by exercise? No chance!

indicators.note: the name Hoon is reworked into a better arrangement

parts.note: Geoff Hoon, the British Labour politician
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Could politician Geoff Hoon get better through a workout? Not a hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoff Hoon was a UK Defence Secretary, a common target in surfaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying there is no hope means there is no chance at all; the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: After taking a turn, upset listener is liable to become infected

indicators.note: the rearranged listener follows the U it takes in front

parts.note: a U-turn, so U stands for a turn

indicators.note: the letters of listener are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An unsettled listener, having taken a turn for the worse, looks set to catch something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsterile is not free of germs, so it is open to infection.

clue.text: Like 8, I long to be travelling with Georgia

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: the words I long are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone longs to travel with Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is INCARCERATING, locking up; GAOL is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Jailing someone is the same as locking them up, the meaning of the cross-referenced entry.

clue.text: Locking up in vehicle, reacting strangely

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the letters of reacting are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone shut inside a car is behaving oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Incarcerating means imprisoning, shutting someone away under lock and key.

clue.text: Spur on first of parrots on perch

indicators.note: only the opening letter of parrots is used

parts.note: a perch or rod is an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.surface: A parrot sits on its perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' suggests a bird's resting place, but it is the old measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod someone is to goad or urge them into action.

clue.text: What the compere will do with stunted beast and how he's removed

parts.note: the runt of a litter is its smallest, stunted animal

indicators.note: the words how he's are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A small animal and a departed presenter in a variety-show setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere presents a show, so he takes charge of it and keeps it running.

clue.text: Oddball wants to perform on dam

indicators.note: in an across clue the piece put on another comes after it

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: An eccentric wants to give a show on top of a river barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an odd or eccentric person, an oddball.

clue.text: Perfect order, but not before bed

definitions.text: Perfect order, but not before bed

parts.words: Perfect order, but not before bed
parts.note: the word that goes before order to mean perfect neatness, and before bed to name a schoolboy prank of short-sheeting

explanation.surface: Everything is tidy, except at bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Apple-pie order is perfect order; an apple-pie bed is a prank in which the sheet is folded so the sleeper cannot stretch out, hardly perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase combines with order to mean neat perfection, but with bed to mean a trick.

clue.text: Fellows get credit for something soothing

parts.note: chaps are fellows, men
on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: Men obtain a loan for a balm.
explanation.definitionFit: ChapStick is a lip balm brand that soothes cracked lips.

clue.text: Keep word about government initially — it's potentially explosive!

indicators.note: the letters of Keep word are turned about into a new order
only the first letter of government is used

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about the government at first: it could go off!
explanation.definitionFit: A keg of gunpowder can explode, and the phrase also means a volatile situation.

clue.text: Call children requiring transport

annotationWithheld.why: Call children requiring transport (4): RING is 'Call', but no parse of 'children requiring transport' holds; the blogger could not explain it and commenters offered only guesses (a hidden word in 'requiring' leaves 'children' unexplained).

clue.text: End of film out now? Cut!

indicators.note: only the final letter of film is taken
the word now is put out of order

explanation.surface: A director calls a halt as the film comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut!' looks like the director's cry, but it is the past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mown grass has been cut, so the participle matches.

clue.text: Readmit tipsy restaurant manager

indicators.note: a drunk word staggers into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk is let back in by the head waiter.
explanation.definitionFit: A maitre d' is the head waiter who runs a restaurant's dining room.

clue.text: (Making a commotion in bed?)

indicators.note: the noise is placed inside the word bed

parts.note: taken as the word bed itself
a racket is a loud din or commotion

explanation.surface: Someone is making a din between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue itself: it is printed inside parentheses, so it is bracketed. 'Making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue sits inside round brackets, so the printed words themselves are enclosed in parentheses.

clue.text: Turn a blind eye to scam fellow employed at the start

parts.note: a con is a swindle
a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college

indicators.note: only the first letter of employed is used

explanation.surface: Someone overlooks a fraud by a colleague who has just been hired.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone wrongdoing is to overlook or tacitly accept it.

clue.text: Passed by, pleased to be moving

indicators.note: the letters of pleased are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to be on the move as time goes past.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has passed by.

clue.text: Bob, a bachelor, carries little weight

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A light bachelor named Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is the verb, to bob up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to move up and down, a synonym for bounce.

clue.text: Shire rents?

parts.note: the word Shire is the letters of hires shaken out of order, as the answer's instruction describes

explanation.surface: A county's rents.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire out is to let something for payment, to rent it.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, he's leaving her on way to the country

indicators.note: what is left is rearranged in a surprising way
the letters of he are taken away from her

parts.note: the letters H and E, which leave

explanation.surface: He walks out on her, unexpectedly, and heads for another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' strikes two letters from the first word, and 'Unexpectedly' scrambles the R left over with ON to give the opening three letters, before the path is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian country.

clue.text: More than one spoke of Roger's plug on TV — two!

parts.note: Roger is the radio word for the letter R
an ad is a TV commercial that plugs a product
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Roger plugs something twice on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoke' looks like the past of speak; it is a wheel spoke, and spokes are radii of the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheel spokes run from hub to rim like radii of a circle, the plural matching more than one.

clue.text: Following little brother, boy takes it on nervously having entered illegally

indicators.note: the boy comes after the brother

parts.note: bro is short for brother
Ken is a boy's name

indicators.note: the words it on jitter into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy follows his kid brother, nervously trying something on.
explanation.definitionFit: Having broken into a place is having entered it illegally, by burglary.

clue.text: Food is taken in by Lawrence

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the letters for Lawrence

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence, the English novelist

explanation.surface: Food is consumed by Lawrence.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food.

clue.text: A miner's pick?

parts.note: the tool a miner chooses and also the man himself; both work underground and excavate

explanation.surface: Which tool does a miner choose?
explanation.walkthrough: A miner is a digger, and his pick is a digger too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a pick and a man who mines dig into the ground.

clue.text: He reversed clamp around the bottom

indicators.note: bind is placed around the turned letters

parts.note: to bind is to clamp

indicators.note: the word He is read backwards

explanation.surface: A man turns a clamp round the base.
explanation.definitionFit: A behind is the buttocks, the bottom.
